answer: The hypothesis is robustly supported: all 256 reported universes show a statistically significant positive Black–White search-rate contrast, with no significant negative results. The estimated standardized contrast ranges from 0.078 to 0.463, although its magnitude is substantially larger in covariate-adjusted models than in unadjusted rate comparisons.
rationale: Positive statistical evidence is completely consistent across the 256 available universes: all 256 are significant and positive, with no indeterminate, unavailable, or significant-negative results. Sensitivity to race definition, stop scope, search outcome definition, missing-data handling, and uncertainty calculation does not reverse the direction or inference; the main sensitivity is the estimator choice, with median effects of 0.082 for unadjusted rates versus 0.409 for covariate-adjusted logistic models.
key_evidence: 256 of 256 universes have statistically significant positive effects; 0 have significant negative effects.
The standardized effect ranges from 0.078 to 0.463, with median 0.241 and interquartile range 0.082–0.409.
Race-definition sensitivity has a 0.0 inference-flip rate and median effects of 0.239, 0.256, and 0.245 across the three definitions.
Covariate adjustment changes the median effect from 0.082 (unadjusted) to 0.409 (adjusted), but has a 0.0 inference-flip rate and 0.0 sign-reversal rate.
caveats: The magnitude is highly sensitive to adjustment for stop composition, so the evidence supports the direction more strongly than a single effect-size estimate.
The supplied effects are standardized; they do not directly report the underlying Black and White search rates.
Statistical significance and a positive contrast do not by themselves establish why the difference occurs.

race_variable_definition.label: Race comparison definition
race_variable_definition.rationale: Which recorded race field and categories define the Black-versus-White comparison?  [found by: direct]

subject_race_black_white.label: Use subject_race categories
subject_race_black_white.description: Retain rows with subject_race == "black" or subject_race == "white"; compare those two groups and exclude all other subject_race values.

raw_race_black_white.label: Use raw_Race codes
raw_race_black_white.description: Retain rows with raw_Race == "B" or raw_Race == "W"; define B as Black and W as White, and exclude all other raw_Race values.

subject_race_with_unknown_as_white.label: Use subject_race with unknowns assigned to White
subject_race_with_unknown_as_white.description: Use subject_race == "black" as Black and combine subject_race == "white" with subject_race == "unknown" or other non-Black categories as the comparison group.

stop_scope.label: Stops included in the estimand
stop_scope.rationale: Does “all recorded stops” mean every row in the dataset or only stops from a Durham geographic or departmental subset?  [found by: direct]

all_dataset_rows.label: All eligible dataset rows
all_dataset_rows.description: Use stops from every county_name and department_name represented in nc-durham-stops, subject only to the selected race and outcome missingness rules.

durham_county_only.label: Durham County stops
durham_county_only.description: Retain only rows with county_name == "Durham County".

durham_police_only.label: Durham Police Department stops
durham_police_only.description: Retain only rows with department_name == "Durham Police Department".

search_outcome_definition.label: Search-rate outcome
search_outcome_definition.rationale: Which column or combination of columns counts as a search?  [found by: direct]

search_conducted.label: Any recorded search
search_conducted.description: Set the binary outcome to 1 when search_conducted == 1 and to 0 when search_conducted == 0.

any_person_or_vehicle_search.label: Person-or-vehicle search
any_person_or_vehicle_search.description: Set the binary outcome to 1 when search_person == 1 or search_vehicle == 1; otherwise set it to 0.

person_search_only.label: Person search
person_search_only.description: Set the binary outcome to 1 only when search_person == 1; set it to 0 when search_person == 0.

vehicle_search_only.label: Vehicle search
vehicle_search_only.description: Set the binary outcome to 1 only when search_vehicle == 1; set it to 0 when search_vehicle == 0.

missing_search_handling.label: Missing outcome handling
missing_search_handling.rationale: How should stops with a missing value for the selected search outcome be handled?  [found by: direct]

complete_case.label: Exclude missing outcome values
complete_case.description: Exclude any retained Black or White stop whose selected search outcome is missing; calculate each race-specific rate using only rows with a nonmissing outcome.

missing_as_no_search.label: Code missing as no search
missing_as_no_search.description: For retained Black or White stops, replace a missing selected search outcome with 0 before calculating rates.

report_missing_as_separate_status.label: Treat missing outcomes as unavailable
report_missing_as_separate_status.description: Do not impute missing outcomes; calculate rates among nonmissing outcomes and additionally report the number and fraction of missing outcomes by race.

confounding_adjustment.label: Adjustment for stop composition
confounding_adjustment.rationale: Should the Black-versus-White search-rate comparison be an unadjusted comparison across stops or adjust for recorded stop and driver characteristics?  [found by: direct]

unadjusted_rate_comparison.label: Unadjusted stop-level rates
unadjusted_rate_comparison.description: For each race, divide the number of stops with the selected search outcome equal to 1 by the number of eligible stops, with no adjustment for age, sex, reason, date, county, department, or officer.

covariate_adjusted_logistic.label: Covariate-adjusted logistic model
covariate_adjusted_logistic.description: Fit a logistic regression for the selected binary search outcome with Black-versus-White race as the focal predictor and subject_age, subject_sex, reason_for_stop, department_name, county_name, and calendar year extracted from date as covariates; report the race contrast from the model.

uncertainty_dependence.label: Dependence and uncertainty calculation
uncertainty_dependence.rationale: How should uncertainty account for repeated stops associated with the same officer_id_hash?  [found by: direct]

iid_two_proportion.label: Independent-stop uncertainty
iid_two_proportion.description: Use a two-sample proportion comparison or equivalent model-based standard error that treats all eligible stop rows as independent.

officer_cluster_robust.label: Officer-clustered uncertainty
officer_cluster_robust.description: Estimate uncertainty with standard errors or a bootstrap clustered by officer_id_hash, allowing stops handled by the same officer to be correlated.

department_cluster_robust.label: Department-clustered uncertainty
department_cluster_robust.description: Estimate uncertainty with standard errors or a bootstrap clustered by department_name, allowing dependence among stops reported by the same department.
